speaker: JACKSON
text: Hmm.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: -- the Secretary of Health and Human Services with appointment authority over the Task Force. That was the question I was answering. And the Fifth Circuit had no need to reach that issue. And this Court also has no need to reach this issue unless it disagrees with our argument on principal officers or unless the Court wants to impose the government's proposed severance  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: In the reply brief --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAGAN
text: Why -- no, please.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: In the reply brief, the government came back with Hartwell. Do you want to address that ca se?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Yeah. Hartwell is not on point because, in Hartwell, the statute required the Secretary of the Treasury to  specifically approve the appointment of that inferior officer. So Hartwell concluded that  was enough to vest the appointment power in the Secretary of the Treasury. We don't have anything like that in these statutes. Nothing in any of the statutes here requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to affirmatively approve the appointment of Task Force members. Now --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: And I guess the government comes back there and says but they have broader authority to -- the Secretary has broader authority to carry out the provisions -- 299(a) and the Reorg Act, they say those together give the Secretary the authority to essentially stand in the shoes, I suppose, would be one way to characterize their argument, of the director. You want to respond to that?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Sure. The Secretary is allowed to appoint the Task Force. We acknowledge that. Anyone is allowed to appoint  the Task Force under the statute. The question is, under the Constitution, who can appoint. The statute doesn't say anything about who appoints. So anybody can appoint them. The AHRQ director appointed them for a time, and that was  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: Well, if you lose your principal -- I think that's important. If you lose your principal officer argument  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Mm-hmm.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: -- so that's the premise, not saying you will  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Right.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: -- but, if you do, and you just said then you could read the statute to allow the Secretary to appoint, that's kind of the end of it.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: No, I don't think so. That's not vesting, all right?  Anyone can appoint under the statute. The Secretary of Energy could appoint. The president could appoint. The AHRQ director could appoint. Someone from the private sector could appoint. The statute doesn't say anything at all about who appoints. No one is vested with the authority because the statute takes no position on who appoints. So  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: Yeah. Okay. And I think I understand your argument. Your  argument's something's got to speak specifically to appointment. The general authorities in the Reorganization Act and 299 are not enough to --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: That's right.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: And that's why Hartwell's different, because Hartwell --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: That's right.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: Yeah. I've got it.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: We have a specific reference in the statute in Hartwell to the Secretary of the Treasury, who must app rove the appointment before it can take effect.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAGAN
text: But is -- is -- is --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: We don't have anything remotely like that here.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAGAN
text: -- is your view that Congress actually wrote a statute without saying who should appoint?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Yes, because they didn't need to work --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAGAN
text: Without even thinking that it was saying who should appoint?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Yes.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAGAN
text: That Congress was leaving this, like, just to the -- whatever they come up with?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Yes, because this was initially established as a purely advisory body. So it didn't matter under -- under the Constitution who appointed them. The Appointments Clause didn't apply to the Task Force when it was first created because it only had advisory powers.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: But, even if purely advisory, to pick up on Justice Kagan's point, it's unlikely that Congress just was throwing it out there in terms of who would --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAGAN
text: I mean, usually Congress thinks that it does things like that, right?  I mean, it would be an odd statute. I doubt you could find another where Congress has set up a board and said, you know -- just not said who should -- who should --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Well, all they said --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAGAN
text: -- who should make up the board?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: -- all they said is that the AHRQ director shall convene the Task Force. And "convene" does not mean appoint, as  Justice Thomas mentioned earlier.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAGAN
text: No.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: JACKSON
text: But it could.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAGAN
text: But, in the absence of anything else, it would be a natural reading to say:  When you're looking at one person and saying he can convene the board, that means -- and there's nobody else out there to actually pick the board members, that means he should also pick the board members.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: He's certainly allowed to pick the board members, Justice Kagan. What we're saying is the statute doesn't forbid other people from appointing. The president could appoint the A -- the members of the Task Force. He could have done that prior to the ACA, and he can do it after the ACA. In fact, we think he's constitutionally compelled now, after the ACA, to appoint them, with the advice and consent of the Senate. There is no statute that forbids the president to appoint.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: GORSUCH
text: Well, if "convene" does mean appoint, then  -- then we do have a problem on -- on an inferior officer theory, don't we?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: There is a problem, yes, because now we have a statute that's requiring the appointment of a principal  officer  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: GORSUCH
text: Well, even on the inferior  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: -- by someone who's not even a head of department.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: GORSUCH
text: Yeah, but even if  -- even if you should lose that argument, again, and we're talking about inferior officers, Mr. Mitchell, if we read "convene" to mean vesting the appointment power in the director, that  --that's  --that's a problem.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: That's a big problem. It means the statute is unconstitutional, and the Court should, therefore, reject any interpretation of the word "convene" that makes it synonymous with "appoint" because that would create not simply a constitutional question but a constitutional violation even --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: Well, that's where you  --that's where you  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: JACKSON
text: But wait. Why?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: -- pull in 299a, which says the Secretary can carry out -- shall carry out the statutory provisions acting through the director. I mean, that's their  response to that, right?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Maybe  -- maybe that works, but, again, the question Justice Gorsuch was asking me is, if (a)(1) is construed to vest the appointment power in the AHRQ director, even the government would agree with us that's unconstitutional.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: That  -- yeah, that alone would be a problem, I totally agree. But then maybe you have to figure out how to fix that problem. And one way that the government points out is, well, the statute itself essentially fixes that problem because it says that the Secretary can carry out the duties of the director.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Maybe that works. But the question, again, under the Article II is where has Congress vested the appointment power. And if Congress has vested it in the AHRQ director, who is not even a head of department, the AHRQ director can't even appoint inferior officers. And the government agrees with us on this much, right?  One thing we all agree on is that the Task Force was unconstitutionally appointed for the 13 -year period that began in March of 2010, when the Affordable Care Act was first enacted into law, through June of 2023, when Secretary Becerra reappointed the Task Force. Everyone agrees that those were unconstitutional appointments, and everyone agrees, I would think, that the recommendations that issued during that 13 -year period cannot be enforced until the Task Force reissues those recommendations after receiving a constitutional appointment. So it's hard for me to understand why the government's suggesting a remedy of severance when, at the very least, we should be entitled to an injunction that restrains the enforcement of --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: Well --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: -- the previously issued Task Force recommendations.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: -- I don't want to belabor it, but I think  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Yeah.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: -- to Justice Gorsuch's point, which is a good one, they're saying constitutional avoidance would say:  Well, don't read it to be the director in isolation. Read the other provisions which give the Secretary authority over the director so that the Secretary can do the convening/appointing, and that solves the constitutional problem.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Yeah, Justice Kavanaugh, I agree that the Secretary is allowed to appoint the Task Force.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: Right.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: And we've never disputed that. The question is  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: And so it's vesting by law under Article II. That's your key point there.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Right. Vested by Congress. Where has Congress by law vested that authority?  And if the statute is vesting the authority in the AHRQ director, that is unconstitutional even if they're inferior officers. And that's why the Court, I think,  has to reject an interpretation of the word "convene" that equates it to "appoint" because  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: GORSUCH
text: And you're saying as well, as I understand it, that if Congress didn't vest it in the director but vested it in the director and the Secretary and 15 other people in between, that's a problem too?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: It's a problem too because these are principal officers. So Congress can't --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: GORSUCH
text: Well, even if they're inferior officers, would it be a problem?  If an inferior  --if the -- if Congress vested the power to appoint an inferior officer in the Secretary plus 15 people, is that permissible?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: I'm not sure. It would -- at the very least, if they had vested it in the Secretary and they also go on to say in the statute but other people can also exercise the power, it still has to be, I think, ultimately, a head of department that  exercises that power, so --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAGAN
text: But what if it's -- what if it's investing it in the director subject to the supervision and control of the Secretary?  So there aren't 14 other people wandering around. It's in the director because  he's the person who convenes, subject to the Secretary, because the statute otherwise gives the  -- the Secretary supervisory control over the director.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: I  -- I don't think that's good enough, Justice Kagan. I think the statute would have to say the Secretary must affirmatively approve the Assistant Secretary or the director's recommendation. That was Hartwell.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: BARRETT
text: But doesn't --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: If the statute went that far, I would agree that's vesting.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: What if it says  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: BARRETT
text: But doesn't that  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: I don't think it  -- I'm sorry.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: BARRETT
text: Go ahead, Justice Kavanaugh. But doesn't that prove the point there are all of these questions, and shouldn't we leave this to the Fifth Circuit  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Yeah.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: BARRETT
text: -- on remand if you lose the principal officer point?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Yes, I do believe that it should be remanded if the Court thinks  it necessary to reach this question. We don't think the Court should reach this question or any court should reach this question because --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: What  --what if  -- just to stay on this point --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Yes.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: -- what if -- Justice Kagan's point, what if it said Secretary or director may appoint?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: If it says the Secretary or director may appoint, then Congress has vested the appointment authority in a head of department. But we would still say that's unconstitutional because they're principal officers. So, if the Court  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: Putting that aside.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: If the Court disagrees with us, if they reject our principal officer argument, that's the question that would have to be resolved by the Fifth Circuit on remand, Justice Kavanaugh.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: GORSUCH
text: I mean, that's -- it's a curious thing just to  --just to continue to say you're -- it's vested in two places. One is constitutional, and the other's unconstitutional.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: But at least Congress has made the vesting in a head of department.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: GORSUCH
text: Well, but  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: And I think the head o f department would have to exercise that authority, first of all.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: GORSUCH
text: Well, what if  -- what if he didn't, though?  What if the Secretary didn't exercise that authority, but the other person did?  I mean, I --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: And --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: GORSUCH
text: We've never had a case like that.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: I don't think there has. I think the Secretary would have to  approve the appointment for it to be valid under Hartwell, and --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: GORSUCH
text: Yeah, I  -- yeah. So  -- so you're saying that under -- under any circumstance  --vested in 15 different places, but, ultimately, for it to be constitutional, it has to be the Secretary who acts?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: The Secretary has to act some in some way, and it may be  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: SOTOMAYOR
text: I'm sorry, you're -- you're --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: Hartwell --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: SOTOMAYOR
text: -- requiring -- if I have an employee and they do something and if I don't like it, I tell them, and if I like it, I leave it alone.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Mm-hmm.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: SOTOMAYOR
text: You want the Secretary to sign a piece of paper that says the director took this action, I saw the  -- I saw the Task Force, I saw the recommendations, I saw him leaving them in place, and that doesn't mean that the Secretary agrees?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: No. We don't think the Secretary has the authority to do any of that.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: SOTOMAYOR
text: You think that the Constitution requires him -- giving Justice Kagan's example -- that the director is subject to the supervision of the Secretary?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Is Your Honor's question asking whether the Secretary has to approve the Task Force's recommendations, or are you  -- is Your Honor asking about whether the Secretary has to approve an appointment to the Task Force?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: SOTOMAYOR
text: Both. Both.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: All right. So, if  -- this is a hypothetical I was being asked from Justice Gorsuch. If there's a statute that vests the appointment power in the Secretary and another person, the Secretary needs to sign off on the ultimate appointment if these are inferior officers  -- and we reject that premise  -- in order for the appointment to be constitutional.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: SOTOMAYOR
text: All right.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Now the -- the other --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: SOTOMAYOR
text: I just  -- I -- I'm having a difficult time understanding.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: Do you  -- you accept Hartwell. You just say this doesn't fall within Hartwell?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: That's right. That's right.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: Okay.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: And, again, all these issues probably should be remanded to the Fifth Circuit if the Court thinks it necessary to reach this point because, number one, the Fifth Circuit didn't resolve the question below. There's very little briefing on this issue. We barely discussed this in our brief. There's a little bit of a more robust discussion in the Solicitor General's reply brief. But also  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: Two pages.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Yeah. This Court has said  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: I was agreeing with you.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: And this Court has said many times:  We are a court of review, not of first view.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: Yeah.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: So I don't think it would be prudent for the Court to rule on that question in the first instance if it thinks it necessary to reach that. And, of course, we  believe it's not necessary for the Court to reach that.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: BARRETT
text: Can I -- can I ask you about your -- your principal argument, the independence point?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Mm-hmm. Yes.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: BARRETT
text: I mean, I guess one thing that I'm struggling with is, you know, as I was suggesting to Mr. Mooppan, your interpretation is very maximalist, and, you know, normally, as Mr. Mooppan said, we try to construe statutes to avoid constitutional questions, not create them.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Right.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: BARRETT
text: And I feel like, you know, there is a way, and during the colloquy with your friend on the other side, a lot of us were asking, you know, ways that you can construe "independence" more narrowly. Why wouldn't we do that for the sake of constitutional avoidance?  I mean, I assume you're going to say, oh, it's not plausible. Is that the  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Well, that's part of the answer. I mean, it's not just the word "independence," but it's also the provision that  says that the Task Force members have to be protected from political pressure to the extent practicable. So that -- that is a maximalist interpretation that's in the statute itself. That language appears there. But I think, secondly, the statute is  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAGAN
text: Well, I don't know. I mean, "to the extent practicable" actually seems non-maximalist to me.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Mm-hmm.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAGAN
text: It suggests that there are limits and --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Sure.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAGAN
text: -- we understand that sometimes it's not going to be possible.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: It may not be possible. You  -- you can't censor people from talking, for example. And if you really wanted to make them completely immune from political pressure, you might have to sequester them the way jurors get  sequestered during a trial and not allow them to read the newspaper or something to that effect. It's not  saying that we should go to these types of extreme measures. But the  -- the reason I don't think constitutional avoidance is even relevant here, Justice Barrett, is because the statute is constitutional no matter how it's construed. Even if the Court were to adopt our view of the meaning of "independent," there is no constitutional problem with the statute. It does not violate the Constitution for Congress to give the Task Force authority to make these preventive care coverage decisions as long as the president and the Senate appoint them  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: Well, I guess --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: -- as principal officers.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: I don't mean to interrupt.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Yes. Please.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: Just coming from a different Article II direction, we usually don't interpret statutes to create independent agencies without some indication that's stronger  than what we have here that this is really protected from presidential or someone else's, Secretary, head of department, removal power.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: I don't know how the language could be stronger, though, Justice Kavanaugh. It's not just the word  "independent," which is what we had in Collins against Yellen, and the Court said that's not good enough to make it independent from presidential removal. It's  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: Well, it could be stronger if it had for -cause protection, and it could be stronger if it didn't have the phrase that Justice Kagan  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Sure.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: -- identified, "to the extent practicable."  Those are two big differences from what you would see normally with an independent agency. And, normally, with an independent agency -- correct me if I'm wrong -- the statutes usually say the president, by and wit h the consent of the Senate, shall appoint.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Right. And there's no specified --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: And that's usually in the statute.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: It is, that's right, because it has to be in the statute. Otherwise --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: And then it says  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: -- there's an Appointments Clause problem.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: And -- and many of them, although not all, say the for-cause removal protection too.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Right. But I think the reason we don't have  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: Right. So all that's missing here.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: That's true, but I think there are -- it's easy to explain why it's missing. This was initially established as a purely advisory body that had no real powers. So that's why they didn't initially say in the statute that the president has to appoint these people with the Senate's advice and consent. It was only when the Affordable Care Act for the first time gave the Task Force real powers as officers of the United States --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: JACKSON
text: Can you speak to the  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAGAN
text: Well, point taken as to what the history is, but still, I mean, we don't go around just creating independent agencies. More -- more -- more often we destroy independent agencies. (Laughter.)

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: That seems to be  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAGAN
text: You know, the idea that we would take a statute which doesn't set up an independent agency  and declare it one strikes me as pretty inconsistent with everything that we've done in this area.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: In terms of construing statutes  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAGAN
text: In terms of  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: -- to maximize presidential influence over the  --over the independent official.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAGAN
text: Yeah. I mean, that, you know, we've -- we've basically said we're not going to read something as putting restrictions on removal power unless it puts restrictions on removal power.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Right. But the problem here, it's not really a question of removal  power, Justice Kagan. The test for principal officer status turns on whether the Secretary can direct and supervise the decisions of these Task Force members. It's the question whether  the principal --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAGAN
text: Well, why isn't removal power enough?  Suppose that there were  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Right.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAGAN
text: -- clear at-will removal power here.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Mm-hmm.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAGAN
text: I mean, we've gone to such lengths to say that that's pretty much -- somebody said it's not the end all and the be all. I think Mr. Mooppan said that.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Right.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAGAN
text: And I don't know. If you read this Court's decisions, it seems often to be the end all and the be all, that the Court has suggested on many occasions  that removal power is really the essence of control. If you  have it, you have control. If you don't have it, you don't have control. Now, as you know I'm sure, on -- on a number of occasions, I've said that that  understanding of removal power is not realistic --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Right.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAGAN
text: -- at least in certain contexts. But the Court has said it again and again. So why doesn't it get you, if not a hundred percent of the way there in a context like this, pretty near there?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: I think that argument would have more force if it weren't for the opinion in Arthrex. If we were litigating this case 10 years ago before the Arthrex opinion, I think that would have a lot of -- that would be a very powerful reason to say these could be inferior officers. But, if you look at the Arthrex opinion, pages 15 and 16, where Arthrex catalogs all the ways in which the PTO Director can influence the decisionmaking of these administrative patent judges in an informal way, without the formal ability to review their decisions, and then the Court says not only is that not good enough, it actually says that aggravates the problem. This is not the solution; it is the problem because it blurs the  lines of accountability and it undermines the transparency that the Appointments Clause is supposed to provide. You know, again, if Arthrex wasn't there, I think we would have an interesting discussion about whether the test for principal officer status should be this formalistic test that Arthrex sets forth or whether we should have more of a hard-nosed legal realist look at the actual powers that the Secretary can exert to influence the Task Force. But Arthrex really, I think, makes it hard for that argument to get off the ground.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: JACKSON
text: Mr. Mitchell, can I ask you about the interval?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Yes.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: JACKSON
text: Because we don't just have potential at -will removal power here. We have something in this statute that seems to me to be fairly unusual, which is the requirement that the Secretary establish this minimal interval after the recommendation is made before they come -- it comes into effect.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Right.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: JACKSON
text: So can you speak to why that doesn't have some indicia of secretarial control that we can look to when we try to understand the relationship between the  Secretary and these members and their recommendations?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: I think it has the opposite implication, Justice Jackson, because 300gg-13 specifically addresses the Secretary's role vis-- vis the Task Force, and as Justice Kavanaugh suggested earlier, it only allows the Secretary to determine when these preventive care provisions are to take effect.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: JACKSON
text: No, I understand  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: So  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: JACKSON
text: -- but it does so for a reason. I mean, if you're right that these are principal officers who are making binding recommendations, I guess I'm struggling to understand what the point of deferring them or allowing the Secretary to intervene and defer them for at least a year, what is -- what is the point of that?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: The point of that is it's very hard for insurers to change their coverage requirements in the middle of a plan year. So the minimum interval is set at one year. That's the minimum so the insurance companies can plan ahead for the next  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: JACKSON
text: But Congress could have done that by statute without the Secretary being involved. They gave the Secretary some authority to establish an interval, so the Secretary's doing work.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Right.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: JACKSON
text: Mr. Mooppan says, during that interval, the Secretary can not only delay the recommendations but can also, in his view, take some steps as to the constitution of the Task Force, perhaps even in communication with them regarding those steps having been done because they made certain recommendations with  --with respect to which the Secretary disagrees. So I guess I'm just trying  -- I mean, it doesn't necessarily suggest that really this is only a time -related thing. The Secretary's getting involved. He's making decisions. Why  doesn't that give us some basis for interpreting this to be a statute in which there is secretarial control?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: We dispute all those claims Mr. Mooppan made about what the Secretary can do during that minimum time interval because the statutes guarantee the Task Force's independence. What Mr. Mooppan is describing where the Secretary can put pressure on the Task Force to pull down a previously issued A or B rating is not consistent with the statutory guarantee.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: JACKSON
text: But the statute doesn't have specific blocks, and so what I'm  -- what I guess I'm -- I'm going back to this notion of how should we be reading this statute. You dispute that the Secretary can do all of those things, but the statute doesn't say he can't. And so why would we read the statute to prevent the Secretary from exercising the control that is necessary to make it constitutional in this situation?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Because it doesn't make the statute constitutional for all sorts of reasons. May I answer, Mr. Chief Justice?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: ROBERTS
text: Sure.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: It doesn't make the statute constitutional, Justice Jackson, because, number one, they're still principal officers because they have unreviewable  discretion when it comes to decisions not to impose an A or B rating. Number two, even if Your Honor's proposed reading of the statute makes the Task Force members into inferior officers, Congress has not vested the Secretary with appointment power over the Task Force, so they're still unconstitutionally appointed. And, number three, Your Honor's proposed reading of the statute still does not fix the problem that occurred from March of 2010 to June of 2023 when even the government acknowledges the Task Force was unconstitutionally appointed during that 13 -year window of time. And all the preventive care coverage mandates that were issued during that time should not be enforceable until the Task Force members receive a new appointment that is  constitutional and they reissue the A or B ratings in response to that constitutional appointment.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: ROBERTS
text: Thank you, counsel. Justice Thomas? Justice Alito?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: ALITO
text: Would you comment on Mr. Mooppan's just  -- argument that a distinction can be made under his understanding of what the Secretary can do between pressure to get rid of a recommendation and pressure to adopt a recommendation in the first place?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Any kind of pressure, Justice Alito, is incompatible in our view with the statutory guarantees of independence. I don't see how that distinction can be reconciled with the text of a statute that not only guarantees the independence of the Task Force members and their recommendations but also says that the Task Force and their recommendations has to be immunized from political pressure to the extent practicable. I just don't see how that distinction could be squared with anything in the text of the statute. I think what Mr. Mooppan is trying to do is salvage some role for 299b-4(a)(6) because it's not plausible, I think, even on the government's view to allow the earlier enacted statutes, such as Section 202 and the  Reorganization Plan, to completely swallow up these later-enacted guarantees of independence. So they're trying to draw some line. But there's nothing in the text of the statute that can provide an anchor for the distinction he  --that he's trying to draw.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: ALITO
text: Suppose it were ultimately -- suppose it is ultimately decided that the statute implicitly confers the appointment power on the Secretary and that -- and then how much more of the statute would have to be jettisoned in order to make it constitutional?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: I don't think any --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: ALITO
text: Like the setup constitutional?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Yeah. None of the statute needs to be jettisoned in order to make it constitutional even under our reading of the statute. If the Court decides that Congress has vested the Secretary with appointment power over the Task Force, the appointments are still  unconstitutional in our view because they're principal officers. They have to be appointed  by the president and the Senate no matter what. But, if the Court even rejects that view, there's still the problem that the Task Force was appointed by the AHRQ director for 13 years between 2010 in March and June of 2023, and there has to be some remedy issued for those admitted constitutional violations.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: ALITO
text: So that would be -- that would be for the -- what was done before Secretary Becerra. What about going forward? What would need to be done?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Going forward, it will depend on whether the Court thinks these are principal officers. If the Court thinks they're principal officers, then they have to be appointed by the president and the Senate as well.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: ALITO
text: Suppose we thought that they were inferior officers.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: If the Court thinks they're inferior officers, there should be a  remand, in our view, to the Fifth Circuit to rule on the question whether Congress has vested the Secretary of Health and Human Services with appointment power. I don't think it's appropriate for the Court to decide that issue based on how cursory the briefing is.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: ALITO
text: Well, suppose that  -- suppose we do that, the Fifth Circuit goes back and says that, or we tackle the question and we say that the statute vests -- vests the appointment power in the Secretary. Then what?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Then there has to be some remedy or --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: ALITO
text: And what  -- that's what I'm asking. What would the remedy be?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: ALITO

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAGAN

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAGAN

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Right.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAGAN
text: And -- and also, Congress is saying to the people who  -- you know, who -- who do supervise and who have discharge powers over them:  You too should think about the fact that this system works best if the Task Force members are treated as independent, but it's -- it's hortatory. case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Well, even if Your Honor read s the statute that way, they're still principal officers under Arthrex because, under  that view that Your Honor is describing of "independence," there's no authority in the Secretary to formally review and formally  reverse the decisions the Task Force is making in either direction. And that's what Arthrex says is key. There may be informal ways the Secretary can influence the Task Force, such as removal or threatened removal or other types of tactics, but Arthrex discusses all these types of informal  means of influence -- again, pages 15 and 16 of the opinion -- and it says that's not good enough.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAGAN
text: Okay. So then I'm going to say then it  --then your argument depends on a pretty aggressive read of Arthrex  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAGAN
text: -- because I thought Arthrex said:  We're dealing here with adjudicators. We're not dealing with every circumstance, every scenario. You know, we're  dealing here with a particular kind of officer.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: I just  --I don't think that's an aggressive reading at all because Arthrex says the touchstone for principal officer status is whether there is formal review available of the relevant official's decisionmaking. And even under the government's construction of the statutes, the only formal review that they're providing is formal review of an affirmative decision by the Task Force to issue an A or B rating. They admit that the Secretary can't reverse the Task Force if it makes a decision in the opposite direction, a decision not to impose an A or B rating. I mean, that alone is enough to make them principal officers even under the SG's view and even under Your Honor's proposed interpretation of the word "independent."  At the end of the day, when you go back to Section 300gg-13(a)(1), it is the Task Force recommendation that matters. That is what is binding on insurers. It is not the Secretary's decision that can bind insurers. So, even if the Secretary were to say: I hereby disapprove this Task Force recommendation, that's useless when it comes  to Section 300gg-13(a)(1) because what matters is what the Task Force says. It's not what the Secretary says.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAGAN
text: Thank you.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: GORSUCH
text: -- which is I didn't see that in  -- in this case.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Right.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: GORSUCH
text: So what do we do about it?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Well, I'm happy to answer Your Honor's question, but, again, it's not properly before this Court because it's not in the scope of the QP. The government did not seek certiorari on the question. And at no point anywhere in the briefing or in  Mr. Mooppan's oral presentation today has the government asked this Court to reverse that part of the Fifth Circuit's ruling. But the ruling is nonetheless correct because the only entity that has the power to impose preventive care coverage mandates is the Task Force. The Secretary's role is only to determine when those coverage mandates take effect. So for the Secretary to go out and say: I hereby ratify the Task Force recommendations, that has no more legal force than if I were to produce a memo that says I ratify the Task Force recommendations. I don't have any authority to impose preventive care coverage mandates either. Neither does the Secretary. So the document has no force  --that's what the Fifth Circuit said in its opinion, and that's completely right. The other reason is notice an d comment. The Fifth Circuit did not reach that issue. But this is undoubtedly a substantive rule. It's clearly a rule. And it's a substantive rule as well because it's imposing binding legal obligations on private insurers. It's prescribing law and policy. So it has to go through notice and comment unless some exception applies. Maybe the good cause  exception if the government wants to argue for that. But, again, they 've waived this entire issue, so I don't think they can possibly make that type of argument now about how an exception to notice and comment might kick in.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: It is  -- it is more powerful than both of those individuals you mentioned because that's  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: Under your theory -- under your theory, yeah.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: -- that is how -- it's not my theory, Justice Kavanaugh. It's how the statute is written.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: Well, I  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: It says -- it says the Task Force shall be independent and shielded from  political pressure to the extent practicable. It's hard for me to see stronger language than that if Congress is trying to create an --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: This goes back to the history. You're  --I mean, when that was originally drafted, that  --they weren't binding.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Right. And I don't think Your Honor should be surprised that Congress would write the statute this way because it's perfectly consistent with this Court's current doctrine. They are not exercising executive power. So Myers and those line  --and all those lines of cases about how the president has to remove executive officers --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: What are -- what are they exercising?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: They're exercising quasi-legislative power. It's not quasi-judicial. They're not adjudicating anything. But they cannot enforce the law against anyone. They are making recommendations that have binding effect under another statute. That's quasi-legislative power. And it's a multi -member agency. It's not headed by a single director. So the  holdings of Seila Law, Collins against Yellen, none of that applies here. This is perfectly constitutional under the Court's current doctrine  --

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: KAVANAUGH

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Right.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents

speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell

speaker: JACKSON
text: No, but wait.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Okay.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: JACKSON
text: This is important.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Please.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: JACKSON
text: Because this is the circularity, right?

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: Jonathan F. Mitchell
text: Right.

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
speaker: JACKSON
text: That if you come back and you say the reason why I'm right that there's not formal review under Arthrex is because we have an independence provision that has these people operating independent of the Secretary or political pressure, then I'm back to Justice Kagan, but that's not what the independence provision means. case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents

case_name: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Secretary Of Health And Human Services, Et  Al., Petitioners, V. Braidwood Management, Inc., Et Al., Respondents
